theory.title: Predicciones y posibilidades futuras
theory.explanation: Usa will para predicciones que consideras bastante seguras y decisiones; may, might o could para posibilidades; y be likely to + infinitivo para desarrollos probables. Usa unless (a menos que) y as long as (siempre que) para expresar condiciones.
theory.tip: Will expresa una predicción más segura; may/might/could indican posibilidad; likely to indica probabilidad.

content.passage: Experts believe that international exchange will continue to grow. More people are likely to study languages online, and small communities may attract visitors who want authentic experiences. Unless historic places are protected, some traditions could disappear. However, as long as people remain curious and respectful, cultural exchange will create new opportunities. Online projects might also help people understand one another without travelling long distances.

items.prompt: Predict how people will learn languages in the future.
items.modelAnswer: In the future, people will probably learn languages through a mix of online lessons, conversation groups and virtual exchanges. Technology may make practice more accessible, but speaking with real people will still be important.

items.prompt: Describe how travel may become more sustainable.
items.modelAnswer: Travel may become more sustainable if trains replace some short flights and hotels use less energy. Visitors could also choose local businesses and stay longer in one place instead of taking many short trips.

items.prompt: What could attract visitors to small communities?
items.modelAnswer: Small communities could attract visitors by offering walking routes, local food and cultural events. People may enjoy learning traditional crafts or meeting local producers. Good transport links would make these places easier to reach.

items.prompt: Talk about a tradition that is likely to remain important.
items.modelAnswer: I think the tradition of sharing a special meal with family will remain important. Even if lifestyles change, people will still want moments to celebrate together and pass stories between generations.

items.prompt: Explain how international teams might work in the future.
items.modelAnswer: International teams might work across different time zones using online meetings and shared digital spaces. They could bring together people with different skills, but clear communication will be necessary.

items.prompt: Predict what a local festival will probably do next year.
items.modelAnswer: Next year, the local festival will probably include more workshops and activities for children. The organisers may invite artists from nearby towns and create a quieter area for visitors who prefer smaller events.

items.prompt: What may happen unless historic places are protected?
items.modelAnswer: Historic places may be damaged unless they are protected and maintained. If local communities receive support, they could preserve important buildings and explain their history to visitors.

items.prompt: Explain what can happen as long as people stay curious.
items.modelAnswer: As long as people stay curious, they can learn from different cultures and build friendships. Travel, books and online conversations could all help people understand perspectives beyond their own.

items.prompt: Talk about how online exchanges could connect people.
items.modelAnswer: Online exchanges could connect students who live in different countries. They might practise languages, compare school life and work on shared projects. These experiences could make international friendships easier to develop.

items.prompt: Make five predictions using will, may, might, could and likely to.
items.modelAnswer: People will probably use more digital tools to learn languages. Travel may become greener, and small festivals could attract more visitors. Historic sites might disappear unless they are protected. These predictions are possible, not certain.

content.audioTranscript: A: How was the cultural exchange? B: Great. The students stayed with a local host family. A: Did they learn about local traditions? B: Yes, and they practised the language every day. A: Did they attend the town festival? B: They did. The whole community was involved. A: How did the visitors behave? B: They showed respect and made new friendships.
